This tutorial uses ordinary QMD and YAML to offer authored explanations,
wording and support. First render it, then change one default and render again.
No model, catalogue, learner account or author-written JavaScript is needed.

## 1. Render and preview

Install the extension using its
[README](https://github.com/kai-prince-sfhea/generative-websites#install-from-github),
then copy this `example.qmd` into your consumer folder. For a local installation,
change the filter selector to `generative-websites` as the README explains.

Use your editor's Render/Preview controls, or:

```sh
quarto render example.qmd
quarto preview example.qmd
```

You should see the **Choose reviewed alternatives** controls and the **Sets**
task below. With JavaScript unavailable, the labelled authored alternatives
remain readable. Core preferences appear first; open **More reviewed preferences**
for other available axes. Source/review declarations remain separately inspectable.
Nothing is downloaded from an AI provider.

## 2. Choose one option at a time

Change **Exposition** to **advanced**. Then change **Terminology** to
**technical**, then open **More reviewed preferences** and change **Scaffolding**
to **expanded**. Each control selects existing
reviewed text; changing one does not infer your knowledge or alter another axis.
The common task stays fixed. **Restore author defaults** resets the choices.

::: {.learning-preferences}
### Choose reviewed alternatives

Try the three independent choices. Source/review inspection shows which authored
versions were supplied; it does not establish independent review.
:::

The review fields in this original synthetic tutorial demonstrate syntax.
Replace the reviewer and revisions after checking your own content. Use
`review="candidate"` on an object still being drafted.

:::: {#sets .adaptive-object concept-id="urn:example:concept:sets" revision="sets-v1" label="Sets" context="urn:example:context:sets" review="author-reviewed" reviewed-by="Example fixture declaration"}
### Sets {#sets-title}

**Common task:** For $A=\{1,2\}$, decide whether $1\in A$ and $3\in A$.
Explain your choices. Every alternative uses this same set and question.

::: {.learning-variant group="explanation" axis="exposition" value="introductory" default="true" revision="intro-v1" review="author-reviewed" reviewed-by="Example fixture declaration"}
#### Introductory explanation

A set is described by its listed members. This set contains one and two.
Check each proposed member against that list before explaining your choice.
:::

::: {.learning-variant group="explanation" axis="exposition" value="advanced" revision="advanced-v1" review="author-reviewed" reviewed-by="Example fixture declaration"}
#### Advanced explanation

Membership in this finite set is decided by checking the displayed elements.
One is listed and three is absent; these observations apply to the stated set.
:::

**Available wording:** [Plain wording: a collection.]{.learning-variant group="wording" axis="terminology" value="plain" default="true" revision="plain-v1" review="author-reviewed" reviewed-by="Example fixture declaration"} [Technical wording: a set.]{.learning-variant group="wording" axis="terminology" value="technical" revision="technical-v1" review="author-reviewed" reviewed-by="Example fixture declaration"}

::: {.learning-variant group="support" axis="scaffolding" value="standard" default="true" revision="support-v1" review="author-reviewed" reviewed-by="Example fixture declaration"}
#### Standard starting prompt

Check each proposed member and state your reason.
:::

::: {.learning-variant group="support" axis="scaffolding" value="expanded" revision="expanded-v1" review="author-reviewed" reviewed-by="Example fixture declaration"}
#### Additional scaffold

Read the listed elements aloud or write them on separate lines. Compare the
first proposed member with the list, then repeat for the second. Keep the given
set unchanged.
:::
::::

## 3. Change the author default

At the top of this QMD, change only:

```yaml
defaults:
  exposition: advanced
  terminology: plain
  scaffolding: standard
```

Keep those lines inside the existing `generative-websites` mapping with its
current indentation. Render again and refresh Preview. **Exposition** should
start at **advanced** while wording and scaffolding keep their own defaults.
You have changed a starting preference, not the shared task or its review.

Next, edit a variant's prose. Review the revised passage and common assumptions,
then update that variant's `revision` and the object's `revision`. Keep stable
IDs while changing visible labels. Copy a group to add your own approved choices.

## 4. Keep a native document

```sh
quarto render example.qmd --to docx
```

The Word document uses the declared axis defaults and the same common task,
without browser controls. `page-url: example.html` records the corresponding
HTML destination; update it if you rename the QMD/output. Neither output infers
mastery or turns a declared review into a proof.

## 5. Try a small activity

The YAML at the top names this activity and its existing `sets` source. Its
parts below are ordinary QMD. In Preview, choose **Record a visit**, reveal the
hint, then save a private reflection. This task has no automatic checker: any
completion is explicitly your own report. Nothing is stored on the device until
you choose the separate Remember action, and no model is needed.

:::: {.learning-activity #membership-activity}
::: {#membership-objective learning-role="objective"}
Explain one membership decision for the common set.
:::

::: {#membership-task learning-role="task"}
For $A=\{1,2\}$, explain whether $3$ belongs to $A$.
:::

::: {#membership-hint learning-role="hint"}
Compare $3$ with each listed element.
:::

::: {#membership-solution learning-role="solution"}
$3$ is not a listed member of $A$.
:::

::: {#membership-reflection learning-role="reflection-prompt"}
Which comparison helped you explain your decision?
:::
::::

Change only the hint's wording, update the activity revision after review, then
render again. The public task stays readable in Word and without JavaScript.
A saved old report can become incompatible when the delivered parts change; its
checks and reflections are private reports, not proof or demonstrated learning.

## 6. Inspect an optional reasoning or symbol candidate

The README now gives an ordinary QMD/YAML recipe for a complete controlled
`Claim:` paragraph marked as a scenario given, rule or goal. Start in inspect
mode, render, check the exact source/role mapping and copy its current review
YAML before a problem download becomes available. Goals and answers never become
givens; the Sandbox still owns actual checking. This tutorial does not enable
that additional feature or require a second copy of its logical statements.

Its WAI-Adapt recipe similarly starts with an existing readable label such as
“Help”. Annotation-only mode needs no image; the optional original local helper
uses your rights-declared PNG only after native inspection, review and an explicit
Show symbols action. You do not calculate the image hash. Reset symbols restores
the ordinary text presentation. This partial project symbol-set pilot is not a
claim of familiar AAC vocabulary or universal helper support.

## Next steps

The [README's advanced reference](https://github.com/kai-prince-sfhea/generative-websites#reviewed-adaptation-and-publication)
covers all eight independent axes, structured activities/private progress,
controlled statement review, explicit cross-page journeys, finite practice, typed assertions, authored
language pages, daily/weekly reports, selected offline reading and editable-source
exports. Optional transfers/storage have their own boundaries.

For a later reasoning exercise, that reference also explains ordinary YAML
`sandbox` problems and `.learning-sandbox` panels. Readers can inspect an
explicitly selected Thread JSON file, keep its exact bytes, or attach a checked
reading route to a source-bound capsule. Imported proof and completion labels
remain reported and unverified; this tutorial does not require a Sandbox,
reasoning file, model or additional setup.

The separate repository source `advanced.qmd` demonstrates the retained two-view
route interface with four objects, alternative preparation, hints and an
explained solution. Copy and render it separately when useful; rendering this
tutorial does not automatically create that guide page.

## Optional standalone number-entry software

The README's **Optional local Numbas 11 activity** section explains how to
prepare a separately obtained standalone folder with the installed command,
inspect and copy its review map, and expose explicit Load/Unload controls.
This tutorial bundles no Numbas software or question collection and does not
load an activity when rendered. Keep a readable native prompt, review the
question/software notices and host CSP, and use normal Render Project.

The paired public fictional paragraphs below illustrate paragraph context, a
referent, negation, and unchanged code/math. This example is not a competent
bilingual certification. Use only author-selected public text here; private
data belongs outside repository and QMD files. Keep the original beside a candidate while reviewing meaning. Render this page
again and inspect the comparison and YAML pins below. Nothing here invokes AI
or grants translation approval. The README explains optional JSON import,
